title: SPT N-Values by Depth and Boring — PP-2 Site
description: Standard Penetration Test (SPT) N-values recorded in Borings BH-PP2-01 through BH-PP2-04. Tests performed per ASTM D1586 using an automatic hammer with calibrated energy ratio of 60% (CE = 0.97–1.05 confirmed by energy measurement). Split-spoon sampler (1.375 in ID, 1.5 in OD). N-values reported as blows per foot (last two 6-inch increments of 18-inch drive). NR = No Recovery (rock encountered); R = Refusal (>50 blows/6 inches on rock). Values in Layer 2 (4–12 ft) reflect stiff to very stiff alluvial clay; Layer 3 (12–23 ft) reflects medium dense to dense alluvial sand.

title: Natural Moisture Content Results — PP-2 Laboratory Testing
description: Natural moisture content determinations per ASTM D2216 on representative split-spoon and Shelby tube samples. Moisture content expressed as percentage of dry soil weight. Values for Layer 2 (alluvial clay) are near the plastic limit indicating stiff to very stiff consistency. Values for Layer 3 (alluvial sand) increase below the groundwater table (13.5–14.2 ft bgs).
notes: SS = Split-spoon sample (ASTM D1586); ST = Shelby tube (thin-wall undisturbed sample, ASTM D1587). ST samples used for consolidation testing; moisture contents from adjacent trimmings. Average Layer 2 moisture content = 20.4%; range 18.2–23.6%.
source: WGC Report 2018-GEO-0093, Table 4-1 and laboratory data sheets (Appendix B)

title: Atterberg Limits and USCS Classification — PP-2 Laboratory Testing
description: Atterberg limit tests per ASTM D4318 (multi-point fall-cone method for liquid limit; rolled thread method for plastic limit) and USCS classification per ASTM D2487. All samples from Layer 2 alluvial clay. Activity = PI / clay fraction (% < 2 micron by hydrometer). Linear shrinkage measured per AS 1289 Method 3.4.1. All samples plot above A-line on Casagrande plasticity chart confirming CL classification.
notes: Average LL = 38.0%; average PI = 18.0%; average Activity = 0.87 (normal activity, consistent with illite–montmorillonite mixed clay mineralogy). All samples plot on or above A-line between CL and CH boundary; none exceed LL = 50 threshold for CH. Activity values < 1.0 indicate inactive to normal clay, consistent with Challis Volcanic weathering products dominated by 2:1 clay minerals.
source: WGC Report 2018-GEO-0093, Table 4-2 and laboratory data sheets (Appendix B)

title: One-Dimensional Swell and Consolidation Test Results — PP-2 Alluvial Clay
description: One-dimensional swell and consolidation tests per ASTM D4546 (Method B: constant volume swell pressure followed by axial loading) and ASTM D2435 for consolidation parameters. Undisturbed Shelby tube samples from Layer 2 alluvial clay. Swell measured at initial field moisture content under in-situ vertical stress before wetting. OCR computed from ratio of preconsolidation pressure (Casagrande graphical method on e-log p curve) to in-situ effective overburden.
notes: Free swell measured under simulated in-situ overburden stress after flooding specimen with distilled water. Swell pressure measured at constant volume (Method B) then specimen loaded to determine compression curve. e0 = initial void ratio at start of test. OCR = σ'p / σ'v. All specimens show OCR = 4–5, consistent with desiccation overconsolidation in semi-arid climate. Cc and Cr values from e-log p curves in compression range. Cα measured during secondary compression stage at high stress (8,000 psf) to capture long-term creep behavior.
source: WGC Report 2018-GEO-0093, Table 4-3 and consolidation data sheets (Appendix B)

title: Corrosion Test Results — PP-2 Alluvial Clay Samples
description: Corrosion characterization tests on three alluvial clay samples from Layer 2. Soil electrical resistivity per ASTM G57 (4-electrode Wenner method). Soil pH per ASTM D4972 (pH meter, 1:1 soil:water suspension). Water-soluble sulfate per ASTM C1580 (ICP-OES). Water-soluble chloride per EPA Method 300.0 (ion chromatography). NACE RP-0169 corrosion classification applies to buried metallic structures. ACI 318-19 sulfate exposure class per Table 19.3.3.1.
notes: NACE RP-0169 resistivity classification: > 10,000 Ω·cm = Mildly Corrosive; 2,000–10,000 Ω·cm = Moderately Corrosive; < 2,000 Ω·cm = Severely Corrosive. ACI 318-19 sulfate exposure: S0 < 150 ppm; S1 = 150–1,500 ppm; S2 = 1,500–10,000 ppm; S3 > 10,000 ppm. Chloride levels (180–310 ppm water-soluble) are below FHWA bridge threshold (500 ppm) but warrant epoxy-coated rebar for elements with direct soil contact. pH 7.2–8.1 indicates slightly alkaline conditions, moderately protective for embedded steel.
source: WGC Report 2018-GEO-0093, Table 4-4 and corrosion laboratory reports (Appendix B)

title: Unconfined Compressive Strength (UCS) Test Results — Challis Volcanic Rock Core
description: UCS tests per ASTM D7012 Method C on NX-size (54.7 mm diameter) core specimens from BH-PP2-03 and BH-PP2-04. Specimens trimmed to L/D = 2.0–2.5 with flat, parallel ends. Axial strain measured by bonded resistance strain gauges and LVDTs. E50 = tangent modulus at 50% of peak stress. Poisson's ratio from lateral/axial strain ratio at 50% peak. Failure modes: AS = Axial Splitting (brittle); SF = Shear Fracture; MF = Mixed (shear + tensile). All tests at room temperature; specimens tested at lab air-dry moisture content.

rows: Highest UCS at site; intact fresh tuff
Mixed mode; intact but with micro-crack

statistics.ISRM_classification: Moderately Strong (R3) to Strong (R4) Rock (25–100 MPa range)
statistics.design_basis_note: Design UCS = mean - 1σ = 6,638 - 1,050 ≈ 5,588 psi; rounded to 5,500 psi for conservative socket friction design. End-bearing calculation used geometric mean of lower quartile specimens.

source: WGC Report 2018-GEO-0093, Table 4-5 and rock testing data sheets (Appendix C)

title: Indirect Tensile Strength (ITS / Brazilian Test) Results — Challis Volcanic Rock Core
description: Brazilian indirect tensile strength tests per ASTM D3967 on NX-size core discs. Specimens trimmed to diameter/thickness ratio of approximately 2:1 (L/D ≈ 0.5). Load applied diametrically at constant displacement rate of 0.2 mm/min. ITS = 2P / (π × D × t). Failure mode: STE = Straight Tensile (central crack); DT = Diagonal Tensile (sub-diagonal crack); IR = Irregular. Test temperature 68°F ± 2°F.

statistics.notes: UCS/ITS ratio of ~9.7 is consistent with brittle volcanic rock (typical range 8–15 for ignimbrite). Tensile strength used in Hoek-Brown criterion as σ_t = ITS_mean in rock mass strength classification.

source: WGC Report 2018-GEO-0093, Table 4-6 and rock testing data sheets (Appendix C)

title: Rock Core Recovery and RQD Summary — PP-2 Cored Borings
description: Rock core recovery and RQD measurements for all core runs in BH-PP2-03 and BH-PP2-04. Core recovery = (length of recovered core / length of core run) × 100%. RQD = (cumulative length of pieces ≥ 4 inches / core run length) × 100%, per ASTM D6032. NX double-tube core barrel (54.7 mm core diameter). Rock type is Challis Volcanic welded rhyolitic ash-flow tuff. Weathering grades: W-IV = Highly Weathered; W-III = Moderately Weathered; W-II = Slightly Weathered; W-I = Fresh.

rows: Highly to moderately weathered tuff; clay-filled joints; orange-brown oxidation; fragmented near top
Slightly weathered; fresh phenocrysts; two sub-vertical joints at 85° dip; thin (1–2 mm) calcite joint fill
Fresh to very fresh devitrified tuff; no open joints; excellent core quality; longest pieces 280–340 mm
Highly weathered near top-of-rock contact; disintegrating to sand-size at very top; core quality improves with depth
Transition from slightly weathered to fresh; two joint sets identifiable in oriented core; apertures < 0.5 mm
Fresh ignimbrite; moderate jointing (RQD 70%); one zone of micro-cracking likely related to stress relief during coring
Fresh; highest core quality in BH-PP2-04; thin pyroclastic layer visible at 31.8 ft depth; no significant joints

statistics.Hoek_GSI_estimated: 50–60 (Fair to Good rock mass, jointed but not highly fractured)
statistics.notes: RQD values in weathered transition zones (CR-1 and CR-4 tops) are reduced by fragmentation and mechanical disturbance during drilling. Design RQD = 45% (lower bound, used conservatively for rock mass classification in socket friction reduction). Average RQD in fresh rock ≈ 70%.

source: WGC Report 2018-GEO-0093, Table 4-7 and core logging sheets (Appendix C)

title: Drilled Shaft Installation Summary — PP-2 Pump Bay (March 2019)
description: Summary of drilled shaft installation observations recorded by WGC geotechnical inspector during construction. All 6 shafts installed on March 14–15, 2019 using Bauer BG 18H rotary drilling rig. 24-inch diameter temporary casing through full alluvial soil depth. Rock socket drilled with tri-cone rock bit and 24-inch core barrel. Concrete placed by pump from ready-mix truck batch loads. Inspector: M. Thornton, WGC; Contractor: Pacific Drill, Inc.
